newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina passes patent confidentiality law.
newsitem.headline: Argentina passes patent confidentiality law.

text.p: The Argentine Congress on Wednesday passed a confidentiality law that will give foreign companies additional patent protection.
The law bars dissemination of technical information on a new product for five years after it is registered.
Extra patent protection, especially for pharmaceuticals, has been requested repeatedly by the United States and European countries.

Also, in a effort to fight tax evasion, the Senate passed a law enabling the tax collection body, DGI, to close shops that fail to give receipts and to fine consumers up to $2,500 for failing to show receipts when requested by inspectors.
Meanwhile, in the lower chamber, a bill to privatize Argentina's 59 airports could not be debated due to lack of quorum.
